notes._summary: Approved cmark-gfm 0.29.0.gfm.13 divergence baseline after issue #144. Of the 58 semantic / 29 visual failures recorded on main, the parser/renderer fixes in this change (GFM table thead/tbody + align attribute, task-list trailing-space normalization via shared list-child renderer, GFM bare-URL/email autolink postprocess with image-alt and code-node skipping, GFM single+double-tilde strikethrough, embedded-HTML-in-table-cell via coherent inline-to-HTML serialization, GFM tagfilter for the Disallowed Raw HTML / HTML tag filter sections, the GFM footnote section renderer under options.gfmFootnoteStyle, footnote-definition indented-continuation capture in the Rust parser, and per-case autolink gating for the CommonMark-core Autolinks section) resolve 44 semantic / 25 visual cases. The 14 semantic / 4 visual cases below remain and are tracked here as documented divergence rather than regressions; each is either a deliberate spec-correct stance, a parser-level limitation tracked as future work, or an out-of-scope rendering target.
notes.spec-0398: Emphasis: cmark 0.29 emits flat output for `__foo, __bar__, baz__` where the CommonMark emphasis algorithm (delimiter runs, rule of 3) mandates nesting, so Supramark's spec-correct parser emits `foo, bar, baz`. Because `font-weight: bolder` is relative, the nesting compounds the weight and renders visibly heavier than cmark's flat output — a real ~0.09% pixel divergence, not anti-aliasing. cmark 0.29 is not uniformly flat, though: it nests in spec-0378/0416, so a renderer-level flatten shim regresses those. Matching cmark here would require reimplementing cmark 0.29's spec-divergent emphasis algorithm in the parser, sacrificing spec-correctness; parser is left spec-correct. See issue #144 (emphasis divergence).

Disallowed Raw HTML: GFM tagfilter escapes disallowed block-level tags at the point of emission, but this case additionally needs active-formatting-element reconstruction across the `

notes.extensions-0020: Autolink crash-safety edge case `(_A_@_.A` renders as the cmark-gfm internal `<IGNORE>` sentinel. This is a cmark-gfm implementation detail, not a real rendering target; tracked as an excluded case.
notes.extensions-0023: Footnotes: the GFM footnote section renderer (options.gfmFootnoteStyle) plus the Rust parser's footnote-definition indented-continuation capture now resolve this case VISUALLY (the definition's blockquote / indented code / paragraph children render inside the trailing `<section>` with the correct backref). It remains in the semantic failure list because the AST projection used for the semantic comparison does not hoist definitions — only the production web renderer does, mirroring extensions-0024.
